answer_leak: PASS — PromoGame.tsx never calls bestPlanSet/planFit before confirmation; `win` is computed only from `confirmedPlan` (set exactly once, at confirm time) via sessionWin. Card order is session.order (shuffled per newSession call), so position never encodes correctness.
brute_force: PASS — selection is a single-value radio (`selected: PlanId | null`, only one plan can be selected at a time — no multi-select exists in the type or the UI). Confirm is guarded by `!selected || !allOpened` and, once pressed, `phase` moves to 'result' and stays there — there is no button or code path that returns to 'select' within the same PromoGame mount. Re-attempting requires leaving and re-entering the Q1 experience from the world map, which starts an entirely new `newSession()` (fresh RNG) — same behavior as every other Q1 game in this codebase, not a reach_mix-specific bypass. gameplay-qa-reach-mix.mjs's `always_pick_*`/`random_pick`/`name_match_only` checks (all <0.5, matching design-sim.mjs exactly) confirm no strategy short of genuine comparison reliably wins.

notes: v1 found and fixed one real CSS bug during manual QA that unit tests/gameplay-qa could not have caught: `position: sticky` silently fails to stick anywhere in this app shell (.app-frame's overflow-x:hidden implicitly computes overflow-y to 'auto' per the CSS spec, but .app-frame never itself scrolls since its height is min-height:100dvh — the page/body scrolls instead — so a sticky descendant is anchored to a box that just moves with the page). Switched to `position: fixed` + a useLayoutEffect-measured spacer div, verified genuinely sticky via live scroll + getBoundingClientRect. v1 also found and fixed stale legacy-mechanic copy in src/data/content/townEvent.ts (mission/discoveryEcho/seeds still described 'combine reach methods' rather than 'compare 3 plans') that the design-review pipeline had no visibility into, since it lives in application content data, not a q1-pipeline design artifact. impl-review-r1 (FAIL 68) then caught a second, more serious instance of the SAME content-data blind spot: resolution.title (also outside the design-artifact chain) asserted actual audience reach — fixed in v2. impl-review-r1's remaining findings (missing visual flourish, non-closable cards, undersized body text) were genuine implementation gaps against the already-approved spec, not new design questions, and are fixed in v2.
